segments: Asking for help isn’t weak.
The emperor of Rome said so himself.
“Do not be ashamed to be helped. Like a soldier storming a wall, you have a job to do.”
Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 7.7
cite
If you’re limping, lean on someone. Then keep climbing.
Send this to a brother who’s struggling in silence.
They got away with it. You didn’t.
Socrates would tell you that you won.
“It is worse to do wrong than to suffer wrong.”
Plato, Gorgias 469c
cite
The man who cheats you damages himself. Stay clean.
Send this to someone who got burned.
You didn’t choose your family. Or your city. Or your time.
Marcus Aurelius didn’t either. He wrote:
“Love the people fate has brought you together with, and do it with all your heart.”
Meditations 6.39
cite
Stop wishing for a different hand. Play this one with love.
Send this to the people you’re stuck with.
You’re looking for it everywhere but here.
Marcus Aurelius pointed inward:
“Dig within. Within is the wellspring of good, and it will always flow if you keep digging.”
Meditations 7.59
cite
The good man you’re looking for is a decision away.
Follow for one rule a day.
